conceptual assets.information: The instruction words held in the processor-internal ROM or RAM, consisting of the pre-initialized application image or bus-written words; instruction fetches and memory read responses depend on these contents.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The application image or stored instruction words may be security-sensitive and can be exposed through bus_rsp_o.data at line 185 after being produced by the memory read paths at lines 81, 95, 128-131 and 159-162. The RAM implementation accepts bus_req_i.data into memory bytes under request controls at lines 114-125 and 143-154, so an unauthorized write can alter instruction words. The memory contents are required for instruction fetches, and rden gates the returned data at lines 176 and 185, allowing required reads to be withheld.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could read security-sensitive words through bus_rsp_o.data, overwrite fetched instructions through the RAM write path, or suppress required read data through the response-enable path.

conceptual assets.information: The word address selecting which internal memory location is read or written; correct instruction fetches and memory writes depend on selecting the intended location.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The address is computed into addr at line 101 and selects the memory word for reads and writes at lines 116-131 and 142-162, so altering it can redirect an access to the wrong location.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter bus_req_i.addr to redirect a read or write to a different memory word, causing an incorrect fetch or corrupting unintended contents.

conceptual assets.information: The internal decision that identifies a read request and permits the corresponding memory word to appear on bus_rsp_o.data; it has no direct entry or exit port because it is decoded from bus request fields and only gates the response data.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The read-release decision is produced from the request at line 176 and controls whether the response data is presented at line 185, so an unauthorized change can alter the integrity of read-response release.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could force the read-release decision low to suppress required memory reads or otherwise manipulate whether a response word is returned.

considered, not kept.reason: The request strobe, read/write direction and byte enables are access command fields rather than conceptual assets of their own, as shown by their uses at lines 114-125, 143-154 and 176-180.

The acknowledgement only repeats the request handshake at lines 178-180 and the error field is tied to a constant at line 186, so bus handshake copies and constant status do not form separate information.
IMEM_SIZE and IMEM_INIT are build-time values that select memory size and ROM/RAM generation at lines 24-25 and 73-107, so no runtime element can change or withhold them.
clk_i and rstn_i only time or reset the memory and response logic at lines 28-29 and 170-182, and the clocks-and-resets rule excludes them as conceptual assets.
